sections.heading: Keep Salesforce on the shortlist only if…
sections.body:
Evaluator thesis: Shortlist when Mid-market and enterprise sales organizations that need a configurable system of record with strong reporting, automation, and integration depth — and that can fund admin/implementation alongside licenses. beat the migration cost. Counter-signal: Drop when USD list pricing rises quickly: Pro Suite list price Enterprise list price Unlimited list price (annual). Add-ons (Agentforce for Sales from list price Contact us, Revenue Intelligence, Success Plans) increase TCO. outweighs Starter Suite value.

Capability hinge for this product: contact management; lead management; pipeline management; deal management.

Integrations in research: Gmail, Outlook, Slack.

Paid tiers that usually matter in evaluation: Starter Suite, Pro Suite, Enterprise.

sections.heading: Who Salesforce is worth it for — and who should avoid it
sections.body:
Worth it for: Mid-market and enterprise sales organizations that need a configurable system of record with strong reporting, automation, and integration depth — and that can fund admin/implementation alongside licenses..

Avoid if: SMB teams seeking a lightweight pipeline CRM, or buyers optimizing for minimal admin overhead and lower seat cost, should compare Pipedrive, HubSpot, or Freshsales..

If avoid signals dominate, start the alternative path with HubSpot on the same job-to-be-done.

sections.heading: Salesforce price/value and next evaluation step
sections.body:
Prove one real workflow on the documented free/trial path before arguing for Starter Suite.

Tradeoff to accept consciously: Platform power and ecosystem depth vs ease of use and admin overhead.

Next step: run contact management end-to-end, then decide.
